text:
Mateo: Heads up — customer X asked for a compliant archival + legal‑hold flow for EU tenants. Wants: 7yr immutable audit evidence, tenant‑level key separation (BYOK-ish), and export that strips PII. Need product + security + eng alignment before Thurs. Quick spec thoughts below and meeting invite at end.

Mateo: Proposed MVP scope (starter):
- Capture: auth events, model_invocations, config changes, billing/usage events
- Hot index: 90d searchable; Cold archive: 7y immutable object store
- Tenant-scoped keys (customer-managed KMS) for at-rest encryption; server-side envelope keys for platform ops
- Export formats: NDJSON + signed manifest; optional PII redaction step
- Legal-hold: toggle per-tenant that pauses retention/expiry, records chain-of-custody

Priya: +1 on tenant keys. We need a clearer KMS handshake flow (rotation, escrow, emergency-access). Also: pseudonymization vs full redaction requirements vary by jurisdiction — call out EU vs US.

Jordan: Engineering notes: rough ballpark for ingest & index costs if we keep 90d hot index — ~2.5x storage vs pure archive for same events. Search SLA for 90d window: target p95 <200ms for metadata queries, full text queries will be higher. Cold export path can be async (hours).

Casey: From SRE: lifecycle policy idea — daily index shards -> rollover -> snapshot to cold store. Cold store must be WORM/immutable to satisfy "immutable evidence" ask. We can do retention enforcement via background TTL job but legal-hold must flip to preserve flagged tenant snapshots.

Lina: Legal flags: chain-of-custody must include who requested hold/unhold, timestamps, and authenticated admin identity. Exports must include a signed audit trail. Also check local retention laws (Germany can require shorter retention for certain PII).

Sam: Customer success note: Customer X says SOC2+ISO mapping is table stakes. Their procurement wants acceptance criteria doc showing: 1) how audit events are collected, 2) proof of tenant key separation, 3) export runbook, 4) legal-hold controls. They expect a PoC in 6 weeks.

Jordan: Clarify: what exactly qualifies as an "audit event" for the export? Is it raw request/response, truncated response, or only metadata + hashes?

Mateo: Good Q. For MVP let's capture raw headers + request metadata + model invocation IDs. Responses that include user content should be hashed and optionally stored behind tenant key. Exports can contain hashes + pointer to encrypted blob; redaction runs before export for flagged fields.

Priya: We should also require HSM-backed KEKs for EU production. Add rotation policy: 90d rotation with 30d overlap. Document emergency-escrow access: approval flow + signed attestation.

Casey: Implementation sketch:
```
index.lifecycle: {
  hot: {max_age: "90d"},
  warm: {max_age: "180d"},
  cold: {immutable_snapshot: true, archive_after: "90d"}
}
```
Cold snapshot -> object store with WORM flag, store manifest signed by ops key. TTL job consults legal_hold table before deleting.

Mateo: Quick product acceptance criteria draft (for PoC):
- End-to-end ingestion -> searchable in <15m for hot events
- 90d hot search SLA documented and verified with load tests
- Cold archive retrieval runbook + measured retrieval time (async)
- Tenant key proof: demo key provision & rotate flow + audit log
- Export: produce signed NDJSON + chain-of-custody manifest

Lina: Add requirement: audit trail must be tamper-evident (append-only with signatures). If we rely on object store immutability, also keep signed manifests in the audit index.

Sam: I'll share the customer's short PoC checklist with procurement this afternoon. They want owner names for each bullet.

Jordan: Tentative owners: index lifecycle + search: Jordan; export tooling + redaction: Jordan + Priya; KMS integration + key rotation: Priya; legal-hold metadata + UI controls: Mateo + Lina; retrieval SLA + ops-runbook: Casey.

Mateo: Meeting: Thu 11am (inv sent). Agenda: confirm scope for PoC, finalize owners, agree on security controls. Please reply with any must-have items before then.

ops-bot: @channel meeting created: Thu 11:00 — "Archival SLAs & Legal‑Hold — Customer X PoC" (zoom link set)

Casey: I'll own the lifecycle implementation and the retrieval runbook. Will post a draft RFC by EOD Wed. :+1:

Priya: I'll draft a KMS handshake sequence diagram and escalation/escrow checklist.

Mateo: Great. If no objections, we'll roll this into next sprint's scoped PoC. Thanks everyone! :rocket:
